newsitem.title: PERU: Korea's LG Metals to buy into Peru's Condestable.
newsitem.headline: Korea's LG Metals to buy into Peru's Condestable.

text.p: Peruvian copper and cement firm Minera Condestable said Tuesday it intends to sell a package of new shares to South Korea's LG Metals Corporation, allowing it to become an 18.89 percent shareholder.

"Yesterday, in Condestable's Lima offices, the current major partners of Condestable, Mr. Javier Chavez L. and Trafigura Beheer B.V., signed with LG Metals a shareholders' agreement that will allow the participation of the Korean refinery in the Peruvian mining company," a Condestable statement said.

The Peruvian company did not give financial details, but said the deal was intended to give LG Metals a foothold in Latin America while also boosting Condestable's expansion program at its mine and flotation plant.
The Mala mine is located 56 miles (90 km) south of Lima, and the flotation plant has a 1,650-tonne per day capacity.

"This is the first investment of LG Metals in mining production and in South America. The Korean Corporation has an ambitious development plan in this part of the continent, one of which is this investment in Peru," the statement added.
"The agreement will allow the development of a full-scale exploration program of the (Mala) property whose first stage has already begun with geology and geophysics studies."
